rows.description: Fearing risk, a manager forbids all AI use. Staff quietly use personal accounts anyway, creating hidden data leaks that a clear and safe policy might have prevented.

rows.subtype: Approach: sharing prompts and lessons in a team log [Action]
rows.description: Members note prompts that worked and failures, and review them on Fridays, so skills grow across the team instead of staying with a few people.

rows.subtype: Approach: protecting skills and learning of juniors [Thinking]
rows.description: The lead worries that juniors may stop learning fundamentals, so asks them to attempt a task first, then use the AI for review, and to explain the code in their own words.

rows.subtopic: Using AI tools inside a team
rows.subtype: Approach: incident review after an AI-related error [Revision]
rows.description: When an AI-generated report included a wrong number, the team traced how it passed review, added a verification step and updated the policy, treating the tool as a fallible colleague.

rows.subtopic: Using AI tools inside a team
rows.subtype: Approach: being open with clients about AI use [Action]
rows.description: The team tells clients where AI assists in delivery, and confirms what data is not shared with tools, building trust through honesty instead of being surprised later.

rows.description: After a harsh post about a product, the founder waits a day, aware that an angry reply written in the moment usually makes things worse and spreads the post further.

rows.subtype: Approach: separating fair feedback from abuse [Thinking]
rows.description: The person reads the comments and sorts them: valid complaints about bugs, misunderstandings that can be clarified, and pure abuse that deserves no reply and possibly a report to the platform.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination

rows.description: The founder argues point by point with critics and attacks their motives. Screenshots circulate, and the argument draws far more attention than the original complaint.
